name: Review and recall
summary: Retrieve what was learned in earlier lessons from memory so it sticks and is ready to build on.
ways: Last lesson, last week, last term

levels.supplementary: Give a word bank with visuals and offer matching or labelled-diagram recall instead of open writing. Allow extra time and check in after the instructions; fewer items covering the same content.
levels.substantial: Provide a pre-prepared recall sheet (cloze, picture matching or sort cards) and have a teacher or LSO read questions aloud and prompt. Accept oral or pointed answers in place of written ones.
levels.extensive: Run recall one-to-one with real tools, samples or photo cards; the student responds by pointing, selecting or using their communication system. Record responses against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Pre-test with the most difficult questions first; students showing mastery (about 85%) skip the drill and instead write hinge questions or explain why a common wrong answer is tempting.
levels.life_skills: Student recalls by matching photos to real tools or materials, or sorting safe and unsafe pictures, alongside peers and with prompts. Record against their Life Skills outcomes.

name: Instruction
summary: Take in new knowledge through a clear explanation, video or reading, and record the key ideas.

levels.supplementary: Pre-teach key vocabulary with a visual glossary and give guided notes with gaps rather than blank pages. Chunk the explanation, pause videos at set points and check in after each step.
levels.substantial: Supply significantly modified notes: mostly complete, large print, one idea per box with images beside the text. Teacher or LSO re-teaches in a small group and scribes or accepts labelled sketches as the notes.
levels.extensive: Deliver the key content one-to-one using real objects, symbols or the student's communication system, in short blocks. Teach to personalised goals drawn from the same lesson.
levels.extension: Compact the explanation after a pre-test and replace repeated content with a conceptual question (patterns, ethics, change over time) that students investigate and bring back to the class.
levels.life_skills: Teach two or three functional ideas from the lesson using real materials and photo cards, with the student seated among peers. Assess against Life Skills outcomes, not the class notes.

capabilities.name: Literacy
capabilities.detail: Reading and viewing › Understanding texts Speaking and listening › Listening

name: Demonstration
summary: Watch a skill or process shown step by step before trying it yourself.

levels.supplementary: Seat the student at the front with a clear sightline, give a photo step card to follow and warn before machines start. Repeat the demonstration in a small group and check understanding.
levels.substantial: Provide a simplified, large-print step sequence and a video to replay. Teacher or LSO repeats the demonstration individually, one step at a time, with the student handling the equipment.
levels.extensive: Demonstrate one-to-one in a low-noise setting, one step per turn, using objects, symbols or key word sign. Hearing protection and close supervision at all times.
levels.extension: After a verified safety induction, students who show mastery skip repeat demonstrations, tackle the fault-finding version or prepare an advanced technique to demonstrate to others.
levels.life_skills: Student watches from a safe, close position and copies one or two steps with support. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes such as following a demonstrated step safely.

name: Worked example
summary: Study a completed example step by step to see how a task is done and what quality looks like.
ways: What a good one looks like

levels.supplementary: Give a printed copy of the exemplar with the key features already numbered and a short checklist of what to look for. Use a faded example so the student completes the last steps only.
levels.substantial: Provide a simplified exemplar with colour-coded annotations and a matching physical sample to handle. Teacher or LSO talks through each feature and the student responds orally or by pointing.
levels.extensive: Work one-to-one with a real finished sample and a single quality feature at a time; the student indicates the stronger of two samples using their communication system.
levels.extension: Have students rank several exemplars, justify the ranking against the criteria and then write the annotations for an unannotated piece, including what would lift it beyond the A range.
levels.life_skills: Student compares two real samples (finished and unfinished, neat and untidy) and chooses which is better, with prompts, working beside peers. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Exploration
summary: Look at, handle or try out examples and materials to build curiosity and first ideas about a topic.

levels.supplementary: Give a reduced set of clearly labelled examples and a see-think-wonder scaffold with sentence starters. Allow a quieter viewing spot and extra time; preview any excursion with photos or a map.
levels.substantial: Pre-select and pre-print the images or objects and provide a tick-box or picture-choice recording sheet. Teacher or LSO supports viewing, describes visual detail and scribes the student's responses.
levels.extensive: Explore one-to-one through object handling and sensory examples; the student shows preference by choosing between two items or symbols. An adult records responses against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Ask students to curate their own reference set around a concept (a trend, a paradox, a design movement over time) and justify each inclusion to a real or simulated client.
levels.life_skills: Student handles real objects and chooses favourites for a simple collage or likes board, with support and alongside peers. Assessed on Life Skills outcomes such as making and communicating choices.

name: Revision
summary: Go back over a topic in an organised way to strengthen memory and prepare for a test or exam.

levels.supplementary: Provide a part-completed summary sheet, a glossary and practice questions broken into steps with a worked answer first. Schedule short check-ins and note any approved extra time or rest breaks for the test.
levels.substantial: Give significantly modified revision materials: visual summary cards, audio or read-aloud questions and scaffolded answer frames. Revise in a small group with a teacher or LSO most lessons.
levels.extensive: Revise one-to-one in short, highly structured sessions using objects, photos and the student's communication system, focused only on their personalised goals.
levels.extension: Skip rote review after demonstrated mastery. Students write and mark an exam-style question with marking guidelines, or apply the content to an unfamiliar case and evaluate their own response.
levels.life_skills: Student revisits functional content with a photo book or matching game about tools, materials and safety, beside peers. Assessed on personalised Life Skills outcomes, not the class test.

name: Discussion
summary: Share and test ideas by talking with others to deepen understanding and hear other views.

levels.supplementary: Preview the questions, give thinking time and let the student rehearse with a partner or write on a mini-whiteboard first. Provide sentence starters and agree in advance when they will be asked.
levels.substantial: Give the questions the lesson before with visual prompts and a prepared response card. Teacher or LSO supports a small-group discussion and relays or records the student's contribution.
levels.extensive: Student contributes through their communication device, symbols or choice cards with one-to-one support, answering one prepared closed question. Peers are taught to wait and respond.
levels.extension: Pose provocative questions with no settled answer and have students argue from multiple perspectives or lead the Socratic questioning. Ask what makes you say that to demand justification.
levels.life_skills: Student joins the pair or group and answers a concrete question (like or dislike, yes or no, which one) using speech, pictures or gesture. Record against Life Skills communication outcomes.

name: Research
summary: Find, select and record information from sources to answer a question.

levels.supplementary: Provide a source pack at an accessible reading level with key words highlighted, plus a note-taking scaffold and a simple referencing template. Chunk the task into dated steps with check-ins.
levels.substantial: Supply two or three pre-selected, simplified or audio sources and a fact-file frame with picture prompts. Teacher or LSO reads with the student and scribes, or the student uses speech-to-text.
levels.extensive: Research one-to-one from a single image-rich or symbolated source; the student selects pictures or symbols to build a fact page. An adult records choices against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Set an open question that needs original research (an interview, survey or industry contact) and have students weigh conflicting sources and report to an authentic audience.
levels.life_skills: Student finds and sorts pictures on a practical topic (for example, fabrics we wear, tools we use) into a simple poster, with support. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Investigation
summary: Test a question or idea first-hand by collecting and recording evidence.

levels.supplementary: Give a step card with photos, a pre-drawn results table and a prediction sentence starter. Pair with a steady partner, check in after each step and allow extra time to record.
levels.substantial: Pre-prepare and pre-measure the test materials and reduce the recording to ticks, photos or a simple scale. Teacher or LSO guides each step and the student gives conclusions orally.
levels.extensive: The student directs the test while an adult handles the equipment; they observe and indicate results by choosing between two options. One-to-one support and a personalised goal throughout.
levels.extension: Students design their own fair test, choose the variables, analyse multiple variables and critique the reliability of the method. Present findings as a recommendation to a client or manufacturer.
levels.life_skills: Student takes part in a concrete test (which fabric soaks up water, which join holds) and says or shows what happened, with support. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Analysis
summary: Break something into its parts to explain how it works or why it has the effect it does.

levels.supplementary: Provide a part-labelled diagram or analysis frame with a word bank of elements, principles or frames terms and sentence starters. Model one part first, then check in.
levels.substantial: Use a significantly modified scaffold: cloze annotations, picture-matched vocabulary and fewer parts covering the same outcome. Teacher or LSO works through it and accepts oral or annotated-sketch responses.
levels.extensive: Analyse one feature at a time one-to-one using the real object; the student identifies parts by pointing, matching or their communication system. Record against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Apply Kaplan lenses (patterns, ethics, multiple perspectives) or hexagonal thinking to link the parts to a bigger idea. Students justify which factor matters most and why.
levels.life_skills: Student names or matches the main parts of a real product (handle, seam, switch) and what each is for, with prompts. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Comparison
summary: Set two or more things side by side to identify what is similar and what is different.

levels.supplementary: Give a comparison table with the criteria and first row completed, plus a word bank. Limit to two items, allow extra time and check in after the instructions.
levels.substantial: Provide pre-made picture or statement cards to sort into same and different, with the teacher or LSO reading them aloud. Accept the sorted cards, photographed, as the response.
levels.extensive: Compare two real objects one-to-one on a single criterion; the student indicates which is bigger, softer or stronger by choosing. An adult records against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Students set and weight their own criteria, compare across disciplines or contexts (industry and classroom) and argue where the comparison breaks down.
levels.life_skills: Student sorts real items or photos into two groups (same or different, hard or soft) with support, beside peers. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Interpretation
summary: Work out what something means and explain your reading of it with evidence.

levels.supplementary: Provide a see-think-wonder frame with sentence starters and a short glossary for the frame being used. Allow a spoken rehearsal with a partner before writing.
levels.substantial: Give a simplified prompt sheet with picture cues and two or three guiding questions per frame. Teacher or LSO discusses the work with the student and scribes or records their spoken interpretation.
levels.extensive: Respond to the artwork one-to-one through sensory or tactile versions, choice cards and the student's communication system. Record reactions and choices against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Have students interpret the same work through competing frames or as a critic and a curator, then explain how the viewpoint changes the meaning. Publish as a catalogue entry for a real exhibition.
levels.life_skills: Student says or shows what they see and how the artwork makes them feel using picture or feeling cards, with support. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Evaluation against criteria
summary: Judge a product, performance, text, solution or piece of work against set criteria and support the judgement with evidence.

levels.supplementary: Supply a criteria rating scale with each criterion explained in plain language and a sentence starter for the judgement. Model one criterion, then check in.
levels.substantial: Reduce to two or three criteria with a visual scale (faces, stars or ticks) and have the product in hand. Teacher or LSO reads criteria and scribes the student's spoken reasons.
levels.extensive: Student trials the product one-to-one and indicates like or dislike and one reason using symbols or their communication device. An adult records against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Students write their own criteria from user research, evaluate for a specific stakeholder and recommend a redesign, weighing trade-offs between function, cost and environmental impact.
levels.life_skills: Student tries a real product and answers concrete questions (does it work, is it comfortable, would I use it) with picture supports. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

capabilities.detail: Understanding ethical concepts and perspectives › Examine values, rights and responsibilities and ethical norms

name: Idea generation
summary: Come up with many possible ideas quickly before choosing which to develop.

levels.supplementary: Give a design brief starter with image prompts and a thumbnail template with a set number of boxes. Allow thinking time, accept quick sketches or words and check in early.
levels.substantial: Provide a reduced-choice idea kit (image cards, shape templates, material swatches) to combine into ideas. Teacher or LSO prompts and records the ideas; accept collage or spoken ideas.
levels.extensive: Offer two or three concrete options at a time one-to-one; the student chooses and combines them using their communication system. An adult draws or assembles at the student's direction.
levels.extension: Tighten or open the brief with real constraints (client, budget, sustainability). Use forced association or SCAMPER to push for original, risky ideas, then justify which idea best answers the need.
levels.life_skills: Student chooses colours, shapes or materials they like from real samples to build one idea, with support and alongside peers. Assessed on Life Skills outcomes about making choices.

capabilities.name: Critical and Creative Thinking
capabilities.detail: Generating › Create possibilities Generating › Consider alternatives

name: Developing and refining ideas
summary: Take a first idea and improve it through drafting, feedback and changes.

levels.supplementary: Provide templates, underlays or grid paper and a short annotation word bank with sentence starters. Break refinement into numbered steps with a visual step card and extra time on CAD.
levels.substantial: Supply pre-drawn outlines or a part-built CAD file so the student refines rather than starts blank. Teacher or LSO gives frequent individual instruction; accept spoken or recorded annotations.
levels.extensive: The student directs changes one-to-one and an adult draws or operates the software at their direction, with choices made through their communication system. Personalised goals apply.
levels.extension: Require iterations that respond to user testing or expert critique, with each change justified against design principles and the brief. Add advanced techniques once core skills are shown.
levels.life_skills: Student improves one thing about their design by choosing between options (colour, size, decoration) using templates or stencils, with support. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Experimentation
summary: Try out different techniques, materials or approaches and record what happens to inform later choices.

levels.supplementary: Give a photo step card at each station, a pre-ruled record sheet with tick boxes and one variable to change. Seat away from noise and check in after each sample.
levels.substantial: Pre-cut, pre-mark and pre-thread materials and machines so the student trials the technique itself. Teacher or LSO works alongside most of the time; results recorded by photo and spoken comment.
levels.extensive: Student experiences each material or technique one-to-one, with hand-over-hand support or the teacher operating equipment at their direction. Record sensory responses and choices against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Students plan their own one-variable trials, predict outcomes and explain unexpected results. Extend into techniques beyond the unit or combine processes to solve a design problem.
levels.life_skills: Student tries two or three safe materials or techniques with support and shows which they prefer and why. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Modelling and prototyping
summary: Build a quick model, draft or mock-up of an idea to test it and find what needs to change.

levels.supplementary: Provide a visual sequence, pre-marked materials for tricky measurements and a checklist of what the prototype must test. Allow extra time and a quiet bench.
levels.substantial: Supply pre-cut pieces, a jig or a kit so the student assembles and tests. Teacher or LSO gives regular direct support and the student reports fit and function orally or by photo.
levels.extensive: Student directs assembly while an adult handles tools, or uses hand-over-hand support and adaptive equipment. Testing is one-to-one against a personalised goal.
levels.extension: Students prototype to answer a specific question, test with real users, record data and justify changes. Encourage low-fidelity risk-taking and a second iteration, not a neater first one.
levels.life_skills: Student builds a simple mock-up from a kit and checks one concrete thing (does it fit, does it stand up) with support. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Guided practice
summary: Practise a new skill with the teacher's support, which is reduced as confidence grows.
ways: I do, we do, you do

levels.supplementary: Place the student near the teacher, give the step card and check each step before moving on. Chunk into single instructions, written and spoken, and allow extra practice time.
levels.substantial: Use pre-prepared materials (pre-threaded machine, pre-marked timber, starter file) so practice targets the new step. Teacher or LSO works beside the student for most of the session.
levels.extensive: Practise one-to-one with hand-over-hand support, tools preset and additional guards or PPE, or the teacher operates the tool at the student's direction. Personalised goals guide each step.
levels.extension: Release students to the you do stage early after a quick mastery check, then set a harder application of the same technique or a problem with no modelled answer.
levels.life_skills: Student completes selected steps of the technique with physical or visual prompts beside peers, on a simplified practice piece. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Tutorial
summary: Follow a set of written, printed or recorded instructions at your own pace to learn a skill or process.

levels.supplementary: Provide a printed step card with photos beside each instruction and tick boxes. Allow pausing and replaying of video, extra time and scheduled check-ins at set steps.
levels.substantial: Give a significantly modified tutorial: fewer words, one photo per step, large print or captioned and narrated video. Teacher or LSO sits with the student and prompts each step.
levels.extensive: An adult works through a symbol or photo sequence one-to-one, one step at a time, with the student indicating next using their communication system.
levels.extension: Compact tutorials students can already do. They attempt the advanced tutorial, troubleshoot a deliberately broken file or sample, or write a step card for a real class to use.
levels.life_skills: Student follows a short visual sequence of three or four photo steps for a functional task, with prompts. Assessed on Life Skills outcomes such as following a visual procedure.

name: Skill practice
summary: Repeat a skill until it becomes accurate and fluent.

levels.supplementary: Give a skills checklist with a done looks like photo, break practice into short timed blocks and check in after each sample. Remove timed-drill pressure; allow extra attempts.
levels.substantial: Provide pre-marked practice pieces, jigs or guides and adapted tools. Teacher or LSO gives regular direct feedback during practice; evidence is the sample plus a photo, not a written record.
levels.extensive: Practise one-to-one with preset tools, adaptive grips and hand-over-hand support, or direct the teacher to operate equipment where manipulation isn't the outcome. Track progress against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Once the standard is met, stop repetition. Move to the top of the challenge ladder: an advanced variation, a combination of techniques or applying the skill in an unfamiliar material.
levels.life_skills: Student practises one functional skill (threading, sanding, saving a file) on a simplified piece with prompts, working alongside peers. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Making and producing
summary: Use sustained work time to make a product, artwork, performance piece, composition or extended text.

levels.supplementary: Supply a staged production planner with dated checkpoints and tick boxes, plus photo step cards at each station. Seat at a quieter bench, check in each lesson and allow extra time.
levels.substantial: Provide pre-cut or pre-marked components, jigs and reduced-choice kits so the student completes the same project. Teacher or LSO assists for most of each session and records progress by photo.
levels.extensive: The student makes design decisions and directs construction while an adult operates equipment, with hand-over-hand support where safe. One-to-one supervision and personalised goals at all times.
levels.extension: Keep one open project but stretch it: added constraints, a real client or advanced techniques, with decisions justified in the folio. Aim for the Newman Symposium or an exhibition.
levels.life_skills: Student makes a simplified, functional version of the class project using a kit and visual sequence, with support. Assessed against personalised Life Skills outcomes.

name: Peer teaching
summary: Teach a skill or idea to classmates, which strengthens your own understanding.

levels.supplementary: Pair the student with a patient partner, give a step card to teach from and let them rehearse first. Offer the choice of teaching one step rather than the whole procedure.
levels.substantial: Prepare a photo sequence or cue cards for the student to use, with the teacher or LSO supporting the pair. Accept showing the steps rather than explaining them aloud.
levels.extensive: Student shows a peer one step using their communication system or by doing it, with one-to-one adult support. Record against a personalised communication or participation goal.
levels.extension: Students who have mastered the skill produce a tested step card or tutorial for a real audience, anticipating common errors and explaining why each step matters.
levels.life_skills: Student shows a classmate one thing they can do (for example, how to put on safety glasses) with prompts. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Safety induction
summary: Learn the rules and safe procedures for a space, activity or piece of equipment before using it.

levels.supplementary: Provide the safe operating procedure as a photo sequence, pre-teach hazard vocabulary and read safety test questions aloud. Allow extra time and a practical demonstrate-back.
levels.substantial: Use a significantly modified, picture-based safety test and repeat the induction individually. Teacher or LSO supervises closely at every use; the student demonstrates each rule on the equipment.
levels.extensive: Induct one-to-one with symbols and physical modelling, additional guards and PPE. The student uses equipment only with constant, vigilant supervision, or directs the teacher to operate it.
levels.extension: After passing the standard induction, students analyse why each control exists, rank hazards by risk or redesign a procedure or guard. The induction itself is never compacted.
levels.life_skills: Student learns two or three key safety behaviours (PPE on, hands clear, stop and ask) with picture cues and practice. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Risk assessment
summary: Identify hazards, judge how serious they are and decide how to control them.

levels.supplementary: Give a part-completed risk matrix with a hazard word bank and one worked row. Use a labelled photo of the workshop for the hazard hunt and check in after instructions.
levels.substantial: Provide picture cards of hazards and controls to match, with ratings reduced to a three-colour scale. Teacher or LSO reads and scribes; accept the sorted cards as the response.
levels.extensive: Identify hazards one-to-one on the real equipment by pointing or using symbols, choosing safe or not safe. An adult records against personalised safety goals.
levels.extension: Students assess a process they have not been taught, weigh likelihood against consequence, debate competing controls and write the safe operating procedure for others to use.
levels.life_skills: Student sorts photos into safe and unsafe and matches PPE to a task, with support and beside peers. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Impact assessment
summary: Weigh up the effects of a decision, product or event on people, society and the environment.

levels.supplementary: Provide a part-filled stakeholder map or impact table with sentence starters and a glossary. Use a short, accessible case study and model one positive and one negative impact.
levels.substantial: Give a simplified, image-based case study and picture cards to sort into helps and harms. Teacher or LSO reads with the student and scribes the reasons they give orally.
levels.extensive: Explore one concrete impact one-to-one using real objects (for example, rubbish and recycling); the student indicates good or bad using their communication system.
levels.extension: Set a genuine ethical dilemma with no clear answer. Students map unintended consequences over time, argue from opposing stakeholders and recommend a decision to a real organisation.
levels.life_skills: Student sorts pictures of who uses a product and whether a choice is good or bad for people or the environment, with prompts. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Documentation
summary: Record the process and decisions behind your work so progress can be seen and explained.

levels.supplementary: Give a folio page template with photo boxes, prompts and sentence starters, plus a word bank. Build in time each lesson to photograph and annotate; check in at set dates.
levels.substantial: Provide a pre-formatted page where the student adds photos and short captions. Teacher or LSO takes or prompts photos and scribes; accept voice or video log entries.
levels.extensive: An adult photographs each stage and the student selects and orders images one-to-one, adding comments through their communication system. Record against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Annotations must justify decisions against the brief and design principles, evaluate alternatives and propose iterations. Present the process for an authentic audience such as a client or exhibition.
levels.life_skills: Student keeps a simple photo record of what they made, sequencing pictures and adding a word or symbol to each, with support. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Drawing and diagrams
summary: Use drawings and diagrams to show information clearly and accurately.

levels.supplementary: Provide isometric or grid paper, a part-started drawing and a conventions reference card. Chunk into numbered steps, demonstrate each and allow extra time.
levels.substantial: Supply pre-drawn outlines or templates with tools preset (set squares taped, compass fixed, CAD starter file). Teacher or LSO gives frequent individual instruction on each convention.
levels.extensive: The student directs the drawing and an adult draws or operates CAD at their direction; alternatively trace or assemble pre-cut shapes with hand-over-hand support. Personalised goals apply.
levels.extension: Students draw a more complex object or their own design to full standards, choose the most suitable drawing type for a manufacturer and justify the choice.
levels.life_skills: Student traces, matches or measures simple shapes with a ruler or template and labels them, with support. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Informal presentation
summary: Share work or ideas briefly with others to practise explaining and to get quick feedback.

levels.supplementary: Give a cue card with three prompts, time to rehearse with a partner and warning of when they will present. Offer presenting to a pair or small group.
levels.substantial: Allow a pre-recorded video or a presentation to the teacher only, using a prepared script or photo prompts. Teacher or LSO helps rehearse and supports during the presentation.
levels.extensive: Student presents through their communication device, a pre-recorded message or by showing the work one-to-one with adult support. Record against personalised communication goals.
levels.extension: Students pitch to an authentic or expert audience, field unscripted questions and defend their decisions. Give feedback on reasoning and risk-taking, not polish.
levels.life_skills: Student shows their work to a peer or small group and says or indicates one thing about it, with prompts. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Planning
summary: Map out the steps, time and resources needed before starting a task.

levels.supplementary: Provide a part-completed time plan or flow chart with dated checkpoints and tick boxes. Model the first steps, give step cards to sequence and review the plan each lesson.
levels.substantial: Supply the production steps as picture cards for the student to order and a pre-filled materials list to check. Teacher or LSO builds the plan with the student and reviews it most lessons.
levels.extensive: Create a now, next, then visual schedule one-to-one for each session; the student chooses the order of steps where possible. An adult monitors against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Students plan backwards from a real deadline, cost materials, identify the critical path and risks, and adjust the plan when a constraint changes. Negotiate their own checkpoints.
levels.life_skills: Student puts three or four picture steps in order and ticks them off as they go, with support. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Reflection
summary: Think back over what you did and learned to decide what worked and what to do next.
ways: What went well, even better if

levels.supplementary: Give a what went well, even better if frame with sentence starters and photos of their own work to prompt. Allow spoken reflection with a partner first.
levels.substantial: Use a traffic-light or rating-scale sheet with picture prompts and a short conference with the teacher or LSO, who scribes. Accept a recorded spoken reflection.
levels.extensive: Reflect one-to-one using photos of the session; the student indicates liked, didn't like and next using symbols or their communication device. Record against personalised goals.
levels.extension: Students evaluate their process against the brief, identify the decision that most shaped the outcome, explain how their thinking shifted and set their own stretch goal.
levels.life_skills: Student chooses a face or symbol to show how the work went and picks one thing to try next time, with prompts. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Peer & self-assessment
summary: Check your own or a classmate's work against the criteria to see what has been achieved and what to improve.
ways: I love, I wish, I wonder

levels.supplementary: Provide the success criteria as a plain-language checklist with examples and feedback sentence starters. Pair with a trusted partner and model one piece of feedback first.
levels.substantial: Reduce to two or three criteria with visual examples of each. Teacher or LSO guides the student through the work, reads the criteria and scribes feedback given orally.
levels.extensive: Compare the student's work with one photo criterion one-to-one; they indicate yes or not yet using their communication system. Peer feedback is given with an adult supporting.
levels.extension: Students apply the full rubric, justify a grade with evidence, distinguish the top bands and give feedback on how to move the work beyond the A descriptor.
levels.life_skills: Student checks their work against a two- or three-item picture checklist and gives a peer a thumbs up or one positive comment, with support. Assessed against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Collaboration
summary: Work with others towards a shared goal, with each person contributing a part.

levels.supplementary: Assign a clear role with a role card, set group norms and a timeline for each person's part. Choose the grouping carefully and check in with the group at set points.
levels.substantial: Give a defined, structured task within the group and pre-prepared materials for it. Teacher or LSO facilitates the group's meetings and supports the student to contribute.
levels.extensive: Student takes a personalised role with one-to-one adult support, contributing through their communication system or by making choices the group acts on. Peers are briefed on how to include them.
levels.extension: Group like-ability students for a design team challenge with a real client and complex constraints, or give a leadership or project-manager role with responsibility for the brief.
levels.life_skills: Student has a real, concrete job in the group (handing out materials, choosing colours, gluing or pressing) with support. Record against Life Skills outcomes about working with others.

name: Check for understanding
summary: Show what you understand so far so the teacher can decide what to reteach or move on from.

levels.supplementary: Offer a choice of response: tick box, circled picture, labelled diagram or one sentence with a starter. Give thinking time before collecting and check privately rather than calling on the student cold.
levels.substantial: Use a pre-prepared ticket with two or three picture or multiple-choice items read aloud by the teacher or LSO. Accept an oral answer or a demonstration at the bench as the check.
levels.extensive: Check one-to-one straight after the activity using yes/no cards, symbols, gesture or the student's communication device. Record against the student's personalised goal for the lesson.
levels.extension: Add a stretch prompt to the same ticket: what if a variable changed, or why does this hold? Use confident responses to decide who compacts the next lesson.
levels.life_skills: Student shows understanding by pointing to, selecting or doing one concrete thing (for example, picking the correct tool) with a prompt. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Feedback and conferencing
summary: Meet briefly with the teacher about work in progress to hear what is going well and agree on a next step.

levels.supplementary: Give feedback in writing and spoken, as one next step on a slip with a tick box. Hold the conference privately and check back next lesson that it was acted on.
levels.substantial: Conference every lesson with the teacher or LSO, using photos or the work itself and a visual next-step card. Model the improvement, then the student attempts it with support.
levels.extensive: Give immediate one-to-one feedback during the task using symbols, gesture or the student's communication system, linked to personalised goals and recorded each session.
levels.extension: Use the conference to probe reasoning and negotiate a stretch goal or compacting. Praise effort, strategy and risk-taking, and bring in an expert or mentor for critique.
levels.life_skills: Teacher gives one simple, concrete next step with a picture or demonstration and the student tries it straight away with support. Record progress against Life Skills outcomes.

name: Reading and comprehension
summary: Read a text, source or article closely to understand what it says and what it means.

levels.supplementary: Give a shorter or chunked version of the text with key words in bold and a word bank. Read the first section together and check in after each chunk.
levels.substantial: Provide a simplified text with images and three guiding questions, read aloud by an adult or peer. Allow extra time and spoken answers.
levels.extensive: Read a few key sentences aloud with picture support and have the student show understanding by pointing, matching or using AAC. Work one-to-one with an adult.
levels.extension: Use a more complex or contrasting text on the same topic and ask students to weigh up the writer's purpose, bias and what is left out.
levels.life_skills: Read everyday texts such as signs, labels, timetables or instructions with support and show the meaning by acting on them. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

summary: Learn, practise and use the key words of the subject so they can be read, said and written correctly.

levels.supplementary: Limit the list to five words with a picture and a plain definition for each, kept on the desk as a word bank. Check in after the first activity.
levels.substantial: Teach three key words with pictures or real objects and practise by matching word to image. Allow spoken answers and extra time.
levels.extensive: Focus on one or two words linked to real objects or actions, shown by pointing, signing or using AAC. Work one-to-one with an adult and repeat across lessons.
levels.extension: Explore word origins, shades of meaning and how a term changes meaning between subjects, then use the words in a precise explanation.
levels.life_skills: Learn functional words for the topic, such as safety signs, tool names or everyday labels, and match them to objects in the room. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

summary: Turn what was read, watched or heard into short notes in your own words.

levels.supplementary: Give a note template with headings and the first point completed, plus a word bank. Allow extra time and check in after the first section.
levels.substantial: Provide partly completed notes with gaps for key words, and pause the source often. Accept labelled drawings or spoken summaries scribed by an adult.
levels.extensive: Have the student choose or match two or three picture cards that show the main ideas, using AAC or pointing. Work one-to-one with an adult.
levels.extension: Combine notes from two sources, point out where they agree or differ, and reduce the result to the fewest words that still hold the meaning.
levels.life_skills: Record one or two important things from the lesson using photos, symbols or key words, such as a list of steps to follow. Record against Life Skills outcomes.

levels.substantial: Provide a guide with pictures and tick-box or circle answers, and play in very short sections. Allow spoken answers and adult support to record them.
levels.extensive: Use a very short clip or sound with one thing to notice, and have the student respond by pointing, choosing a picture or using AAC. Work one-to-one with an adult.

summary: Work through an unfamiliar problem by choosing a method, testing it and checking the answer makes sense.

levels.supplementary: Give the problem in short chunks with a steps checklist and a worked example to refer to. Allow extra time and check in after the first step.
levels.substantial: Use smaller numbers or fewer steps, supply a part-completed solution and concrete materials or a diagram. Work alongside an adult or peer for the planning step.
levels.extensive: Work on one step of the problem with objects, pictures or a calculator and adult support. Accept a spoken, pointed or AAC response for the answer.
levels.extension: Solve the same problem a second way, then generalise it or change one condition and predict what happens.

levels.supplementary: Give a scaffold with question prompts, a word bank and the first row completed. Use a shorter source or a simplified graph, and allow extra time.
levels.substantial: Use one short source or a single graph with key parts highlighted and read aloud. Offer sentence starters and multiple-choice or matching responses.
levels.extensive: Explore one image, object or simple picture graph with adult support and respond by pointing, sorting or AAC. Focus on one question such as who or how many.
levels.extension: Add a conflicting source or a second data set and judge which is more useful for the question. Explain what further evidence would be needed.

summary: Collect first-hand information at a site outside the classroom by observing, measuring, recording and asking questions.

levels.supplementary: Give a recording sheet with headings, an example entry and a word bank. Pair with a buddy, preview the site with photos and allow extra time at each stop.
levels.substantial: Reduce the number of sites or measurements and use tick boxes, photos or labelled diagrams instead of written notes. Provide adult support and a visual schedule of the visit.
levels.extensive: Take part in one sensory or observation task with adult support and record by photo, object collection or AAC. Plan access, rest breaks and a familiar routine for the day.
levels.extension: Design part of the method, such as the sampling plan, and evaluate how accurate and reliable the data is. Suggest how the method could be improved.

summary: Play a short game that makes you recall, explain or use the content you have been learning.

levels.supplementary: Give a word bank or notes page to use during the game and extra thinking time before answers are called. Pair with a supportive partner and go over the rules with a visual.
levels.substantial: Use a smaller set of questions with picture or multiple-choice answers and remove time pressure. Offer a set role such as scorer or card reader alongside playing.
levels.extensive: Join the game by matching pictures, objects or symbols with adult support, responding by pointing or AAC. Keep rounds short and the routine predictable.
levels.extension: Write the questions or clue cards for the game, including ones that need an explanation or an example. Justify answers instead of only naming them.

summary: Make an original piece, such as a story, poem, melody, movement phrase, scene or artwork, to turn ideas and techniques into something new.

levels.supplementary: Give a planning template with the first section completed, a word or idea bank and a model to refer to. Break the piece into two short parts with a check-in between them.
levels.substantial: Offer a part-made piece to finish, such as a story with the ending missing or a melody with four bars written. Allow spoken, recorded or drawn responses and work alongside an adult for the planning step.
levels.extensive: Create through choice-making: the student selects images, sounds, words or movements from a small set using pointing, objects or AAC, and an adult records and assembles the piece with them.
levels.extension: Add a constraint that raises the complexity, such as a second voice, a shift in point of view or a set structure, and ask for a short statement justifying the choices.

levels.substantial: Provide a scripted or part-scripted role with visual cues, pre-teach the situation and allow a non-speaking role such as recorder or timekeeper. An adult rehearses the role with the student beforehand.
levels.extensive: Take part through a simplified role with one clear action or choice, using objects, pictures or AAC to respond, with an adult alongside throughout.
levels.extension: Take a role with a competing interest or an unexpected complication, then write or speak a short analysis of how the simulation differs from the real process.

levels.extensive: Perform one prepared action, sound, word or switch-activated cue within the group piece, practised with adult support and visual or tactile prompts.
